messages.subject: Maybrook v Helmsworth - first review & strategy
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

I've been through the contract and logs. Headlines:

1. Clause 7.1 (satisfactory quality/fitness) is squarely in our favour - four failures including the crusher write-off.
2. Clause 7.3 says the plant is 'capable of' 320 t/h. They'll argue that's a test figure. Our weighbridge data shows ~210 t/h sustained.
3. THE problem is clause 14.2 - liability capped at 12 months' hire (£222k) and loss of profit excluded. Our biggest head is £742k lost profit. We need a UCTA reasonableness argument.
4. Misrep under s.2(1) is worth pleading - reverses the burden.

I think we lead with the letter of claim and line up a plant engineer. Thoughts on counsel - Harriet Stanford?

Kind regards,
Tom

messages.subject: RE: Maybrook v Helmsworth - first review & strategy
messages.plaintextBody:
Agree on all four. Clause 14.2 is the whole ball game on quantum - get the UCTA point properly pleaded in the Reply when it comes. Harriet is a good shout for the merits opinion; let's instruct after we have the expert's preliminary view. Push hard on the lost-profit causation evidence - Halcyon contract is key.

Proceed with the letter of claim.

Best,
Sarah

Whitfield Carter LLP
